sentences.cn_text: 在社交场合中，与他人进行眼神接触可以表明你正以友好的方式关注对方。
sentences.en_text: In a social situation, eye contact with another person can show that you are paying attention in a friendly way.

sentences.cn_text: 但眼神接触也可能带有对抗性，比如政治候选人在辩论中转向对手，用眼神传递出敌意。
sentences.en_text: But it can also be antagonistic, such as when a political candidate turns toward their competitor during a debate and makes eye contact that signals hostility.

sentences.cn_text: 以下是严谨的科学研究揭示的关于眼神接触的事实：
sentences.en_text: Here’s what hard science reveals about eye contact:

sentences.cn_text: 我们知道，典型的婴儿会本能地凝视母亲的眼睛，而母亲也会回望婴儿。
sentences.en_text: We know that a typical infant will instinctively gaze into its mother’s eyes, and she will look back.

sentences.cn_text: 这种相互凝视是母子依附关系的重要组成部分。
sentences.en_text: This mutual gaze is a major part of the attachment between mother and child.

sentences.cn_text: 成年后，以愉悦的方式注视他人可以是一种表示关注的赞许信号。
sentences.en_text: In adulthood, looking at someone else in a pleasant way can be a complimentary sign of paying attention.

sentences.cn_text: 它能在拥挤的房间里吸引某人的注意。心理学家莫妮卡·摩尔的研究支持了这样一种常识性观点：「眼神接触与微笑」可以传递出可接近性与自信。
sentences.en_text: It can catch someone’s attention in a crowded room. “Eye contact and smiles” can signal availability and confidence, a common-sense notion supported in studies by psychologist Monica Moore.

sentences.cn_text: 神经科学家邦妮·奥扬发现，在一次简短的面试中，通过记录受试者的注视方向证实，催产素激素增加了男性对面试官的眼神接触量。
sentences.en_text: Neuroscientist Bonnie Auyeung found that the hormone oxytocin increased the amount of eye contact from men toward the interviewer during a brief interview when the direction of their gaze was recorded.

sentences.cn_text: 这一现象在一些具有自闭症谱系症状、可能倾向于回避眼神接触的高功能男性中同样得到证实。
sentences.en_text: This was also found in high-functioning men with some autistic spectrum symptoms, who may tend to avoid eye contact.

sentences.cn_text: 其他研究人员正利用先进的脑部扫描方法，探索在直接注视时做出反应的特定脑区。
sentences.en_text: Specific brain regions that respond during direct gaze are being explored by other researchers, using advanced methods of brain scanning.

sentences.cn_text: 借助眼动追踪技术，哈佛大学肯尼迪政府学院的朱莉娅·明森得出结论：眼神接触可能传递出截然不同的信息，这取决于具体情境。
sentences.en_text: With the use of eye-tracking technology, Julia Minson of the Harvard Kennedy School of Government concluded that eye contact can signal very different kinds of messages, depending on the situation.

sentences.cn_text: 在友好情境中，眼神接触或许是联系与信任的标志，但在对抗性情境中，它更可能与支配或恐吓相关联。明森说：「无论你是政治家还是父母，都应记住，若想说服一个信念与你不同的人，一味保持眼神接触可能会适得其反。」
sentences.en_text: While eye contact may be a sign of connection or trust in friendly situations, it’s more likely to be associated with dominance or intimidation in adversarial situations. “Whether you’re a politician or a parent, it might be helpful to keep in mind that trying to maintain eye contact may backfire if you’re trying to convince someone who has a different set of beliefs than you,” said Minson.

sentences.cn_text: 当我们注视一张脸或一幅图像时，视线每次只会停留在一个点上，通常是眼睛或嘴巴。
sentences.en_text: When we look at a face or a picture, our eyes pause on one spot at a time, often on the eyes or mouth.

sentences.cn_text: 这种停顿通常每秒发生约三次，随后视线跳向另一个点，直至图像中若干重要部位如同一系列快照般被依次捕捉。
sentences.en_text: These pauses typically occur at about three per second, and the eyes then jump to another spot, until several important points in the image are registered like a series of snapshots.

sentences.cn_text: 尽管这是当前研究的热门课题，但整幅图像究竟如何被整合与感知，至今仍是未解之谜。
sentences.en_text: How the whole image is then assembled and perceived is still a mystery although it is the subject of current research.

sentences.cn_text: 芬兰研究者贾里·希耶塔宁及其同事发现，在神经质测试中得分较高的人——神经质是一种与自我意识和焦虑相关的人格维度——眼神接触会触发更多与回避相关的脑部活动。「我们的研究结果表明，当人们成为关注焦点时，不仅主观感受不同，其大脑反应也存在差异。」
sentences.en_text: In people who score high in a test of neuroticism, a personality dimension associated with self-consciousness and anxiety, eye contact triggered more activity associated with avoidance, according to the Finnish researcher Jari Hietanen and colleagues. “Our findings indicate that people do not only feel different when they are the centre of attention but that their brain reactions also differ.”

sentences.cn_text: 一项更为直接的发现是，那些在焦虑等负面情绪维度上得分较高的人，注视他人的时间更短，而当他人未直视自己时，他们反而感到更为舒适。
sentences.en_text: A more direct finding is that people who scored high for negative emotions like anxiety looked at others for shorter periods of time and reported more comfortable feelings when others did not look directly at them.

sentences.cn_text: 眼睛的注视是短暂的。
sentences.en_text: Eye fixations are brief.

sentences.cn_text: 人们本能地认为过多的眼神接触是无礼的。
sentences.en_text: Too much eye contact is instinctively felt to be rude.

sentences.cn_text: 眼神接触可以是一种友好的社交信号。
sentences.en_text: Eye contact can be a friendly social signal.

sentences.cn_text: 人格特质会影响一个人对眼神接触的反应方式。
sentences.en_text: Personality can affect how a person reacts to eye contact.

sentences.cn_text: 眼神接触背后的生物学因素正在被深入研究。
sentences.en_text: Biological factors behind eye contact are being investigated.

sentences.cn_text: 大多数人并不习惯与陌生人长时间保持眼神接触。
sentences.en_text: Most people are not comfortable holding eye contact with strangers.

sentences.cn_text: 眼神接触也可能带有攻击性。
sentences.en_text: Eye contact can be aggressive.
